content:
Following this week's announcements of the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone Duo, Apple has begun accepting trade-ins of the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 for credit toward a new purchase. However, the trade-in offer for the iPhone Air is somewhat underwhelming, especially after this week's price increase.

Apple typically waits until new iPhone versions are released before accepting trade-ins of older models. But that isn't the case with the iPhone Air and iPhone 17 — there's no iPhone Air 2 or iPhone 18 yet, with new models not expected until early next year at the earliest.

That said, Apple does want to give iPhone Air and iPhone 17 users a chance to upgrade to the iPhone 18 Pro or iPhone Duo. As a result, both of these iPhones — which are still on sale from Apple but have no successors — are eligible for the trade-in program.

Take the iPhone 17 as an example: after this week's $100 price hike, its starting price is $899, and Apple is offering a maximum trade-in credit of $585.

The iPhone Air also got a $100 price increase this week, pushing its starting price up to $1,099. So what does that extra $200 over the iPhone 17 get you in trade-in value? The same $585 credit. That's genuinely rough.

Apple's trade-in value table almost makes you think it's a $100 calculation error. In reality, Apple is likely pricing based on market demand and component value. Given that the iPhone Air uses virtually the same chip as the iPhone 17 Pro, it's a real disappointment.

In summary, the iPhone Air is now 'worth' $100 more to new buyers — yet its trade-in value, at least according to Apple, is on par with a model that's $200 cheaper. Not a great look, folks.
